name: Samuel Choi
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember the ledger balanced on an ironing board.” People around Juniper Street know Samuel by a small Thursday habit. Samuel knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I found a pencil debt to my mother between two lines about roofing nails.
appearance: Samuel has a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth. Look for a blunt cut just below the ears. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a red windbreaker with one loose pocket corner secured with green thread. In conversation Samuel looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry.
personality: Samuel listens for the familiar version of a story and then for the one detail that changes it. Friends bring problems here when they want to be heard twice.
agenda: To settle the penciled debt to the mother.
family: Bianca Sethi is Samuel’s younger relative by marriage. Samuel asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Bianca remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The quiet verse*, Bianca says, “I wrote the verse about my dad and then decided nobody gets to hear it yet.”
connections: Taylor Beck. They trace the first cleaner's tip back to an unpaid ledger line. Also in the story is Rain Salcedo (founding shareholder).

reactions.situation: A family member wants the ledger locked away
reactions.response: Samuel asks whether the heirs can look at copies without parting with the old ledger.
reactions.asWritten: A family member wants the ledger locked away. Samuel asks whether the heirs can look at copies without parting with the old ledger.

reactions.situation: Smoke appears under a shop door after closing
reactions.response: Samuel alerts the nearest occupied shop, stays outside and writes down when the smoke first appeared.

reactions.response: Samuel keeps the accounts separate until the witnesses have had a chance to meet.
